title: Product frame: Chain Trace — what it shows: A source-to-result view places each material beside the agent step and its contribution, with one primary action, Review result. Navigation: Canvas · Materials · Runs · Memory · Settings. Con
description: A source-to-result view placing each input material beside the agent step that processed it, showing contribution status (Included, Applied, Awaiting, Unproven) with a primary Review result action.

thread.answer:
- A traceability frame showing how an AI system combined multiple sources (image, text, connected notes) to form a single result
- Card-based layout displays each contribution with type (visual context, written context, instruction, suggestion), source, and status (Included, Applied, Awaiting acceptance, Unproven)
- Uses a single accent color (teal) on dark background with subtle icons—visual restraint that helps focus attention on understanding the chain, not the interface
- Each card includes a trace-back capability: pointing back to the source (image, article, note) to verify where that contribution came from
- Primary action 'Review result' is positioned as invitation to validate, not approve automatically—result stays as suggestion until owner accepts it
- Sidebar navigation (Canvas, Materials, Runs, Memory, Settings) keeps context accessible without cluttering the trace view

How to apply:
- Extract the card-based pattern for your own processes: each contribution gets status, explanation, and a way back to its source
- Adopt the single-accent-color approach in dark mode to reduce noise when users need to understand complex multi-step formations
- Create status vocabulary (Included, Applied, Awaiting acceptance, Unproven) that maps to different roles: materials vs. agent suggestions vs. unresolved claims
- Position primary actions near summary explanations—invite decision after showing the chain, not before
- Use icons and brief labels to help users quickly identify contribution type without reading full descriptions

suggestions: Compare how different inputs would change the result
Show which step had most impact on the final output
Export the trace as a checklist or audit trail
